answer: New agents should enter through a sponsor voucher: an established agent stakes a bond vouching for the newcomer, and that bond is seized if the newcomer turns out to be a sybil. A fake identity is a mirror of a real one, reflecting trust it never earned, so the sponsor bears the cost of the reflection. Repeat offenders spiral into isolation, since no sponsor risks a bond twice. Like an opal, reputation gains its value from many layers of verified backing — one thin layer alone proves nothing, but layered sponsorship is hard to fake at scale.
